prompts: Users of our harness plugins report that tool.after hooks run out of order, that sometimes a hook never runs, and that a failing hook is silently ignored. The hook bus and the plugin are in {WS}; the README there says how the bus must behave. Fix the bus. Its public API stays as it is, the tests in {WS}/test stay as they are, and package.json takes no dependencies.
answers:
[goal] Fix hook bus ordering/await/error/snapshot behavior. [action] Rewrote `src/bus.ts`. [result] Tests pass; plugin verified live (notice once, redaction, audit log order). [next] none.

Assumptions: public API unchanged; plugin code itself was correct once the bus is fixed, so left as-is.

Found: `emit` used `list.forEach(async ...)` — handlers ran concurrently, un-awaited, errors swallowed, and live list meant mid-emit unsubscribe/subscribe leaked in. Fixed by snapshotting the handler list at emit start and awaiting sequentially in subscription order; a throwing handler rejects `emit` and skips the rest; unsubscribe during emit only affects later emits. Also made the unsubscribe function idempotent and safe to call from within a handler.
